question.text: The breakeven point for a long put option buyer is:

explanation.text: The Logic: Put BEP = Strike Price - Premium Paid At BEP, the put payoff exactly covers the premium paid. Example: Strike = 17,500, Premium = 177.60 BEP = 17,500 - 177.60 = 17,322.40 At spot 17,322.40: Payoff = 17,500 - 17,322.40 = 177.60 = Premium. Net P/L = 0. The Trap: Call BEP = Strike + Premium (add). Put BEP = Strike - Premium (subtract). Cross-Exam Context: For profit: underlying must go BELOW BEP for puts, ABOVE BEP for calls. Distributor's Pro-Tip: Put BEP = X - P. Profit when spot < BEP.
